key_insight: MACE-based molecular dynamics can reproduce DFT sorption trends for point defects in 2D materials and appears robust even at 300 K.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster high-throughput prescreening of defect stability and sorption behavior, reducing reliance on expensive DFT-only workflows.
method: Simulated 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database.
Ran MACE-accelerated MD at 0 K and 300 K.
Compared adsorption vs. absorption trends against prior high-throughput DFT results.
evidence_signal: Across 17,624 defect structures, MACE reproduced the overall DFT sorption trends at 0 K and showed similar qualitative trends at 300 K.
watch_item: MACE is best used for prescreening; DFT is still needed for accurate quantitative validation and final defect ranking.
paper_title: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
